messages:
ashley: heads-up: latency spike on asia-east-1 GPU pool around 10:02 UTC. Seeing NVLink link flaps and AER messages — inference p95 jumped ~45% :rotating_light:

cory: dash: https://metrics.redwood/shot/asia-east-1/gpu-pool/1749004321 — you can see the NVLink error rate and token latency overlay

maria: grabbing dmesg from rack12-node03 (short):
```
[09:58:12] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Multiple Uncorrected error, severity=Uncorrected
[09:58:12] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 62
[09:58:30] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: root port recovery
[09:59:05] nvlink0: lane 2 down
```

sre-bot: ALERT: NVLINK_FLAP spike detected on asia-east-1/gpu-pool (count=18 in last 10m) — auto-escalate to eng-oncall

ashley: nodes showing repeated flaps: rack12-node03(gpu01/gpu02), rack12-node04(gpu03). Throughput-sensitive tenants impacted (model-serving high batch).

devops: logs show coordinated PCIe resets 09:58–10:01. Example kernel line: `pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: root port recovery; resetting link` — looks like link-level retries then reset.

cory: proposed action: drain rack12-node03 first, move jobs to asia-east-1-burst pool, enable fallback routing to non-NVLink variant (nvlink-disabled) for heavy KV-cache workloads. Start drain now? :thumbsup:

maria: note on cost/constraints: moving to burst/other regions will incur ~20% extra GPU spot delta + possible egress; infra-costs should be pinged if we exceed daily budget. Also check quotas in other racks — free_gpus in region=6.

ashley: can we preemptively shift long-running evals off the pool before eviction to avoid double failures? I'll kick that off.

oncall: executing drain command: `./orch drain rack12-node03 --reason "NVLink flaps / Xid" --by ashley` — action started, node marked draining.

devops: during eviction window Xid events persisted on node03. I recommend immediate reseat of the suspect card (slot B) and re-run memtest + nvlink stress. If reseat doesn't clear, RMA.

cory: opened RMA ticket INFR-3245: https://rma.redwood/t/INFR-3245 (attached logs, dmesg, perf graphs). If RMA needed, schedule after-hours swap to minimize impact.

maria: quick mitigation for serving: reduce batch size on affected routes (set `max_batch_tokens=512`, `prefetch=false`) and drop KV prewarm for models > 2B to limit long-tail stalls.

ashley: monitoring — will update in 30m with drain progress and whether reseat stabilizes link. If flaps persist after reseat, we'll plan RMA + temporary capacity bump. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

cory: FYI — adding a follow-up ticket to infra-playbooks to document this exact NVLink/AER drain flow and cost escalation steps. :memo:
